cases.title: WordCount map tasks killed after retries

groundTruth.cause: One cluster node was disconnected from the network, so tasks could not reach HDFS datanodes on it (NoRouteToHost) to read their input blocks and were killed after retries.
goodNextSteps: Check network connectivity to the datanode address in the errors (ping, routes, switch port, firewall)
Check the HDFS datanode report for dead or unreachable nodes

answer.summary: Map tasks failed due to network connectivity issues or a misconfigured data node address change, both leading to inability to retrieve block data and eventual task termination after retry limits were exceeded. The root cause is likely either a network outage or an unhandled address change in the data node configuration, with the latter being more likely given the specific address change log entry at 21:39:36Z.
missingEvidence: Network connectivity status between 10.190.173.170 and the map task host (MININT-FNANLI5/127.0.0.1) at the time of the incident

hypotheses.cause: A network connectivity issue between the map task and the data node at 10.190.173.170 caused repeated NoRouteToHostException errors, leading to the failure to retrieve block data and eventual task kill after retries.
hypotheses.nextStep: Run a ping and traceroute from the map task host to 10.190.173.170 to verify network reachability and identify any routing or firewall issues.

hypotheses.cause: The data node at 10.190.173.170 underwent a service address change from 10.190.173.170:9000 to msra-sa-41:9000, which the map task failed to detect, resulting in a failed connection and subsequent task kill.
hypotheses.nextStep: Check the data node's configuration and service logs for any restart or IP address change events around 21:39:36Z to confirm if a service migration or restart occurred.
